Asobi Review 1.0 (build 1047) Sep 30, 2026

  • Known issues. Notes the studio already knows about carry a yellow KNOWN tag and are listed under the brief.
  • Already noted here. While you type a note, a line above the field shows what has already been said at that moment, so it can be added to instead of repeated.
Earlier updates

1.0 (build 1045) Sep 30, 2026

  • The review brief. When a review opens, a card titled Before we start may show the studio’s brief: what is already known and what to look at. Click Got it; the yellow BRIEF tag reopens it, and it comes back once if the studio changes it.
  • Tidier Film Lab. The negative and print menus now run the full width of the panel.

1.0 (build 1042) Sep 30, 2026

  • Halation in the Film Lab. Tick Halation for the red glow film gets around bright lights, from light that bounced off the back of the film and exposed the red layer again. Set its strength, size (in microns on the negative, so it holds from a proxy to the original), threshold, hue from red to orange, a second bounce and a soft scatter. It is added to the scene light before the look, as on film, and shows in the viewer, compare, scopes, grabs and exported movies. It saves with the look and travels with the grade.
  • An eyedropper in the tool palette. The color pop-up has an eyedropper: pick a mark color from anywhere on screen, the picture included.

1.0 (build 1039) Sep 30, 2026

  • One color button in the tool palette. In the column as well as the bar, the palette shows the current color as a single button. Click it and the swatches and the custom color open beside it; picking one closes them. The column is shorter for it.

1.0 (build 1037) Sep 30, 2026

  • Words under the buttons. The control bar now names each button (Play, Loop, Notes and the rest), as the web page does. Turn them off with View ▸ Button Labels (⌥⇧⌘B).
  • A horizontal tool palette. The paint tools can sit as a bar along the top instead of a column. The colors then open from a single color button, as on the web. Switch with the button beside the palette’s grip, or View ▸ Tool Palette Horizontal. Each layout remembers where you put it.
  • The palette comes back when you ask. View ▸ Tool Palette now has a shortcut (⇧⌘P) that works wherever you are. The eye menu’s Tool Palette also brings back a palette hidden with P; before, it could show a tick with no palette.

1.0 (build 1035) Sep 30, 2026

  • Clearer drawing tools. The tool icons are bolder and follow the conventions of paint programs: a brush for drawing, a heavy T for text, a solid eraser. The web review uses the same set.
  • Angled wipes cut where the line is. On a wide picture, a wipe set at an angle used to cut at a steeper angle than the line drawn over it. The cut now follows the line exactly, in the app, in frame grabs and on the web. Vertical and horizontal wipes are unchanged.
  • What’s New keeps the recent history. This window now lists the last several updates, not just the latest, so nothing is missed if you skip a few. Reopen it any time from Asobi Review ▸ What’s New in Asobi Review…

1.0 (build 1029) Sep 30, 2026

  • The selection box turns with the marks. Rotate a stroke, line or arrow and the box, its handles and the rotate knob turn with it; scaling a turned selection works along its own sides, as in any graphics app. ⇧ snaps the angle to 15°.

1.0 (build 1026) Sep 29, 2026

  • Scale and rotate marks. A selected mark has handles: drag a corner to scale it in proportion (⇧ frees the proportions, ⌥ scales from the center), an edge to stretch it, and the knob above to rotate a stroke, line or arrow (⇧ snaps to 15°). Line weight stays as drawn; text grows with a corner.
  • Select several marks. ⇧-click adds or removes a mark; ⇧-drag across the picture selects every mark the box touches. Move, scale, recolor or delete them together.
  • The web page does the same, and every seat sees the result.
